name: stack-disclosure
description: Reads response headers for what they give away about the stack: the web server and its version, the language, framework or CMS, the build that is deployed, internal host names and private addresses, framework session cookies, and debugging aids left switched on. Each is recorded as a finding, once per host, with the setting that turns it off. Reading traffic is passive; nothing is held or changed. When the vulnerability check is turned on (off by default), a banner that names a full version is looked up on the NVD API and CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and every known vulnerability becomes a finding graded by its CVSS score — this sends the product name and version (never your targets' addresses) to services.nvd.nist.gov and cisa.gov.

settings.label: Only report banners that name a version
settings.description: Off: "Server: nginx" is a finding as well as "Server: nginx/1.18.0". On: only a banner with a version is. Internal hosts and addresses, build numbers, debugging headers and framework cookies are reported either way.

settings.label: Detectors to skip
settings.description: Detector ids never to report: server_banner, tech_header, app_version, proxy_banner, internal_host, internal_address, bigip_cookie, stack_cookie, debug_header. The README lists what each one finds.

settings.label: Most findings from one response
settings.description: A response whose headers trip more detectors than this is stopped at the cap.

settings.label: Look disclosed versions up for known vulnerabilities (active)
settings.description: Off (default): nothing is sent. On: when a banner names a full version of a known product, the version is looked up on the NVD API and CISA KEV, and each vulnerability becomes a finding graded by its CVSS score. This sends requests to services.nvd.nist.gov and cisa.gov (the product and version only), recorded in the Traffic list. Answers are kept for a day, so a version is asked about once however often it is seen.

settings.label: NVD API key
settings.description: Optional. A free key from nvd.nist.gov raises NVD's rate limit (50 requests per 30 seconds instead of 5), so a run with many versions finishes sooner. Without one the lookups just run slower.

settings.label: Query the NVD API
settings.description: Version-precise CVEs with CVSS scores. On by default when the vulnerability check is on.

settings.label: Use CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
settings.description: Flags which CVEs are being exploited in the wild, and covers appliance products (such as F5 BIG-IP) that NVD can't match by version. On by default when the vulnerability check is on.

settings.label: Only look up a full version
settings.description: On (default): only a banner that names a complete version (all of major.minor.patch, e.g. 16.1.0 or 2.4.41) is looked up, since a two-part release line like 1.18 can't be matched to a CVE reliably. Off: look up whatever version is named.

settings.label: Lowest CVSS score to report
settings.description: A CVE below this base score is not recorded. 0 reports everything; 7 reports only High and Critical. Does not apply to CISA KEV product matches, which carry no score.

settings.label: Most CVEs per version
settings.description: The most findings to record for one disclosed version, most severe first.
